bottom_line: In patients with heart failure and a reduced ejection fraction, dapagliflozin vs placebo reduced the primary composite of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.85).
implications: Based on the reported hazard ratio for the primary composite outcome (0.74; 95% CI, 0.65 to 0.85) and the reported event proportions (16.3% vs. 21.2%) over a median of 18.2 months, the results support that dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death than placebo in this trial population; the report also shows lower cardiovascular death (0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98) and all-cause death (0.83; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.97). The document does not show a significant difference in the prespecified worsening renal function composite (0.71; 0.44 to 1.16).

major_points.text: Phase 3, placebo-controlled trial; 4744 patients with NYHA II–IV HFrEF (≤40%) randomized to dapagliflozin 10 mg daily vs placebo on top of recommended therapy.
major_points.quote: In this phase 3, placebo-controlled trial, we randomly assigned 4744 patients with New York Heart Association class II, III, or IV heart failure and an ejection fraction of 40% or less to receive either dapagliflozin (at a dose of 10 mg once daily) or placebo

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite of worsening heart failure (hospitalization or urgent visit requiring IV therapy) or cardiovascular death.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was a composite of worsening heart failure (hospitalization or an urgent visit resulting in intravenous therapy for heart failure) or cardiovascular death.

major_points.text: Over median 18.2 months, the primary outcome occurred less often with dapagliflozin than placebo (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.65 to 0.85; P<0.001).
major_points.quote: Over a median of 18.2 months, the primary outcome occurred in 386 of 2373 patients (16.3%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 502 of 2371 patients (21.2%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.85; P<0.001).

major_points.text: Cardiovascular death and all-cause death were also lower with dapagliflozin than placebo.
major_points.quote: Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 227 patients (9.6%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 273 patients (11.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98); 276 patients (11.6%) and 329 patients (13.9%), respectively, died from any cause (hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.97).

major_points.text: Findings were similar in patients with and without diabetes.
major_points.quote: Findings in patients with diabetes were similar to those in patients without diabetes.

major_points.text: Adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction, and hypoglycemia did not differ between treatment groups (as stated in the abstract).
major_points.quote: The frequency of adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction, and hypoglycemia did not differ between treatment groups.

guidelines_referenced.quote: Drug doses were individually tailored, in accordance with guideline recommendations.

inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligibility requirements included an age of at least 18 years, an ejection fraction of 40% or less, and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II, III, or IV symptoms.

criticisms.quote: This trial has some limitations. We used specific inclusion and exclusion criteria, which may have limited the generalizability of our findings.
